subject: Dedicated vs Private VPC - data isolation follow-up
messages:
From: Tom Jacobs <tom.jacobs@finsecure.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>
Cc: Asha Verma <asha.verma@finsecure.com>, procurement@finsecure.com
Date: Mon, 3 Aug 2026 10:00:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Dedicated vs Private VPC - initial call follow-up

Hi Marissa 

Thanks again for the call earlier today. Quick recap from our side and a few clarifications so your team can help us determine whether Dedicated capacity will suffice or if we need a Private VPC/on-prem deployment: 

- Requirement: All inference traffic and model context must remain inside our AWS account (no egress to shared Redwood-hosted networks).
- KMS/HSM: We need customer-managed keys for any persisted artifacts (kv cache, logs).
- Control plane: We prefer a private control plane option or a model where control-plane calls do not traverse the public internet.
- Audit logs: Full request/response-level audit logs (token-level retention policy controlled by us) are required for compliance.
- Multi-tenancy: We cannot share GPU hosts with other tenants.

Attached is our internal network and compliance requirements doc for reference.

Next steps: can you confirm which of these are covered by Dedicated (reserved capacity) vs Redwood Private (VPC or on-prem)? Also loop in someone from solutions/security if needed.

Regards,
Tom Jacobs
CTO, FinSecure
[Attachment: FinSecure_network_requirements.pdf (pdf)]

From: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>
To: Tom Jacobs <tom.jacobs@finsecure.com>
Cc: Asha Verma <asha.verma@finsecure.com>, Mateo Alvarez <mateo@redwood.com>, Rachel Kim <rachel@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 3 Aug 2026 14:12:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Dedicated vs Private VPC - data isolation follow-up

Tom 

Appreciate the clear summary and the attachment, that helps a lot. Short answers up front, then a couple clarifying questions so we can route you to the correct technical path: 

- Dedicated (Reserved Capacity): provides isolated GPU pools and per-customer tenancy at the allocation level, but control plane and some orchestration services remain in our hosted control plane. Network egress typically goes via Redwood-managed endpoints unless configured with PrivateLink/VPC peering options.
- Redwood Private (VPC/on-prem): supports a private control plane and customer-hosted data plane (VPC peering or on-prem), can be configured so that inference traffic never leaves the customer's network and keys are managed by your KMS/HSM.

A couple clarifying questions to pinpoint the right path:
1) When you say "must remain inside our AWS account", do you mean absolutely zero outbound connections from the inference hosts to Redwood-managed services, or is an API call to a Redwood control plane over PrivateLink acceptable?
2) Are you open to a Private deployment with a Redwood-managed control plane that is implemented within your VPC (private-control-plane pattern), or do you require a fully air-gapped on-prem install?
3) For KV cache and logs, do you need them to be encrypted with your CMK and stored in your S3 buckets, or would a Redwood-hosted encrypted store with customer-key wrap be acceptable?

Looping in Mateo (solutions) and Rachel (security) to help with the technical and compliance answers. I can set up a 30-min follow-up demo/technical walkthrough this week  

---
Redwood Inference | Developer-first inference for production
https://redwood.ai

From: Mateo Alvarez <mateo@redwood.com>
To: Tom Jacobs <tom.jacobs@finsecure.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>
Cc: Rachel Kim <rachel@redwood.com>, Asha Verma <asha.verma@finsecure.com>
Date: Tue, 4 Aug 2026 09:05:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Dedicated vs Private VPC - data isolation follow-up

Tom 

Jumping in with initial technical guidance based on the list you shared:

- Zero egress option: We support a fully private data plane where inference hosts have no outbound access to the public internet. That can be achieved with Redwood Private deployed in your VPC or on
prem.
- VPC peering / PrivateLink: For customers who want Redwood-managed control plane but keep data plane traffic internal, we offer PrivateLink and VPC peering options that ensure control-plane traffic traverses private networking (no public internet).
- CMK / HSM: We integrate with customer KMS for key management; for HSM-backed keys we can support BYOK with HSM-backed CMKs, but some audit flows require additional validation

Rachel can confirm.
- Audit logs & retention: We can stream request/response audit logs to your S3 (encrypted with your CMK) and provide configurable retention.
- Multi-tenancy: Dedicated capacity is isolated at the GPU pool level (no shared inference VM processes with other tenants), but the underlying hardware may still be hosted in Redwood-managed racks. For strict physical isolation and air-gapped needs, Private on
prem is recommended.

Questions for you to confirm before we recommend a path:
- Do you require the control plane to be hosted in your account (yes/no)?
- Is there an explicit prohibition on any third-party orchestration calls outside your VPC?
- Are you required to have HSM-backed key material stored exclusively in your key vault?

If you can reply with those answers, we can put together a short deployment options doc and an estimated timeline and cost delta between Dedicated and Private. I can also run a quick architecture dial-in this Thursday at 11am PT if that works.

Thanks 

Mateo Alvarez
Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
[Attachment: Redwood_Private_requirements_checklist.xlsx]

From: Tom Jacobs <tom.jacobs@finsecure.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>, Mateo Alvarez <mateo@redwood.com>

Date: Wed, 5 Aug 2026 16:30:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Dedicated vs Private VPC - data isolation follow-up

Marissa / Mateo 

Thanks 

- Control plane: we prefer the control plane hosted inside our AWS account via PrivateLink; fully air
gapped on
prem is not our primary requirement today.
- No third-party orchestration: we cannot have any orchestration calls that transmit raw request/response payloads outside our account; metadata calls to Redwood over PrivateLink are acceptable if they are limited to health/status and do not include PII or request payloads.
- HSM: yes, HSM-backed CMK required for persisted KV cache and any stored logs.

If you can provide a short doc outlining the PrivateLink + Dedicated hybrid pattern (control plane in our account, data plane isolated) and any timeline/cost implications, we can review internally and loop in procurement for contract/po steps.

I'll take the 11am PT slot on Thursday 

please send calendar invite.

Regards,
Tom
